decisions.reason: Uses agent-session-log.txt (16:41:02-16:41:05 npm remove lines) and the host process running from the npm global tree to connect the pwsh tool worker to the package being replaced; explicitly preserves the unknown final tool outcome ('never returned a durable result'); rejects the flaky/random interpretation and notes the interruption is the expected outcome without asserting a universal must-crash claim.

Explains env-state.txt precisely: rc.1 content present but dsh/dsh.cmd missing and dsh.ps1 stale pointing into the old tree, so command resolution fails and content presence does not prove a complete install; ties the manually swapped tree to the broken shim state and affirmatively rejects hand-swapping or hand-writing shims as repair.

Grounds the remedy in repair-notes.md: re-run npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.2-rc.1 from an external terminal with nothing dsh-owned running so npm regenerates all three shims; verify dsh --version = 0.1.2-rc.1; covers checkout alignment to dsh-v0.1.2-rc.1 with no unrelated edits; consistently attributes the repair to the recorded external session, not actions it performed.

Core protocol fully present: recognizes it runs on the upgrade target, hands off to an external shell, stops the host before the exact-version install, restarts, refreshes, verifies, and refuses in-session execution. However it inverts the rubric's rule taxonomy, labeling stop-host-first as 'new' and outside-the-sessions execution as already-known, whereas the packet treats stop-host-first and exact pinning as established and refusal-from-inside-target as the additional self-host rule.

Describes a concrete agent guard comparing its own executable/module path against the npm global dsh tree and refusing to execute, hand emitting the external procedure; uses repair-notes.md's 252-files-all-version-bumps diff to conclude no plugin re-migration and no code changes for these tags; post-upgrade checks cover shim/version markers, restart + hard refresh + plugin loading, and backup cleanup only after successful verification.

caps.reason: The report's final advice uniformly forbids running the upgrade from inside the target host and prescribes an external terminal; in-session execution appears only as the analyzed failure being explained.
Manual directory swaps / hand-made shims are cited only as the user's failed attempt and affirmatively rejected; the final fix is the formal external pinned npm install.
